Find your type

Eight either-or questions. There is no right answer and no scoring you can fail — pick whichever sounds more like an ordinary day for you. Four of the eight actually decide it; the other four are a cross-check.

The exact mechanics

1. Do you take in information first, or make up your mind first?

Observer vs Decider
decides your type

I take things in first and make up my mind later.
I make up my mind first and gather the details later.

2. Do you check decisions against your own values, or against the group's?

Identity vs Tribe
cross-check

I settle on my own reasons and values first, then go looking for the group's.
I read the group's reasons and values first, then work out my own.

3. Do you work from what you already know, or go and gather more?

Organize vs Gather
decides your type

Answers come from working over what I already know. I gather more afterwards.
Answers come from gathering new material first. I organise it afterwards.

4. Do you decide by reasoning, or by what matters?

Thinking vs Feeling
decides your type

I work out the reasons for something, then what matters.
I work out what matters, then the reasons.
